cutLine: Revision 1.9.28 scope P10 is implemented at its front-end and measured execution boundaries: void-pointer arithmetic uses byte scale in every named form; signed and unsigned 128-bit assignment targets and compound-assignment type propagation are accepted without opening 128-bit interpreter execution; wide enumerations select one completed-list target type; __attribute aliases __attribute__; and declaration-free translation units are valid. The tree is green at 1038/1038 workspace tests (1037/1037 all-target tests), exact 128/128 and 22/22 layout corpora, and a locked/offline no-local replay. Raw preprocessing remains 16/16, dual-oracle clean parsing moves from 9/16 to 10/16, and dashboard regressions are zero. Stage F1 remains OPEN on 12 parser lanes across six units: six E2202 invalid-initializer-type, four E2001 undeclared-identifier at __builtin_frame_address, and two E1303 enumerator-value-is-not-an-integer-constant observations across the two oracle streams.

specAmbiguities: The acceptance contract opens GNU asm in scope F but its outOfScope field still lists inline asm. Scope F and the architecture-owner instruction were followed; the stale field was not silently rewritten.

Section 10.1.15 permits integer operands of differing width but does not state whether GNU __int128 value semantics are in this profile. The frozen oracle table and implementation tests cover at most 64-bit inputs; 128-bit checked-arithmetic operands remain unfrozen.

Section 10.1.15 requires p to point to a non-_Bool integer and says the result is stored through p, but does not explicitly freeze whether pointer-to-const is rejected or which diagnostic and span apply.

Section 10.1.16 assigns E2914 at the operand span for two named failures, but does not freeze the code/span for duplicate qualifiers, a labels section without goto, or an unresolved goto label. For an unknown template %[name], no corresponding operand span exists; this implementation anchors it to the template.

Section 10.1.16 says C-HIR preserves asm losslessly including spans, but does not enumerate whether source aliases and string-fragment spellings must survive in addition to decoded semantic text and component spans.

Section 10.4 lists __BASE_FILE__ and __TIME__ among dynamic macros, while the frozen five-capability red window and scope-P execution instruction open only __COUNTER__. Those two dynamic macros remain outside this red window rather than being silently specified here.

Section 10.4 requires unknown pragmas to be counted in the dashboard, but the tracked dashboard schema has no ignored-pragma field or aggregation path. The preprocessor exposes a deterministic per-translation-unit count; no dashboard field was invented.

Scope line P says raw lanes no longer stop on E0104 without qualifying the message, while the execution authority specifically required E0104 Unknown compiler at zero. The scope-P publication had zero Unknown-compiler lanes but fourteen different E0104 cpucaps-overflow lanes; P2 has since moved all fourteen onward without rewriting that historical contract.
P4.C11-reference-scope: section 10.4 cites C11 6.4.8 while the complete preprocessing-token production is in C11 6.4.

P4.header-name-and-other-paste: section 10.4 enumerates identifier, punctuator, literal and pp-number paste results but does not say whether header-name or other may be synthesized by two nonempty operands; the accepted tests cover placemarker preservation and do not invent that rule.

P4.dollar-classification: scope P4 lists dollar among stray characters while section 10.4 limits it to outside identifiers and the GNU lexer accepts dollar as an identifier character; no standalone-dollar classification is claimed.
H-STALE-EXCLUSION: section 10.1.7 still says statement expressions are outside the profile while section 10.1.11 covers them.
H-JUMP-IN-DIAGNOSTIC: jumping into a statement expression is malformed but no diagnostic code or exact message is assigned.
H-STATIC-LITERAL-RELOCATION: the required file-scope pointer initializer needs a static relocation/provenance representation that revision 1.7 explicitly deferred.
H-COMPOUND-GLOBAL-IDENTITY: no deterministic unnamed compound-literal global identity or GlobalKind is specified.
H-READONLY-STATIC: E3014 is broadened to const file-scope literals while the memory sections still define read-only storage as string-literal-only.
H-JOIN-ARG-CARDINALITY: the stated single value block argument does not say how it composes with mandatory live-local, mem<all>, or world block arguments.
H-SCALAR-DESIGNATOR-DIAGNOSTIC: the plan requires E2906 on scalar designators but the normative E2906 condition names only missing fields and fixed-bound indexes.
H-DESIGNATOR-ICE-DIAGNOSTICS: invalid designator index and range constant expressions have no assigned diagnostic.
H-RANGE-EVALUATION-COUNT: side-effect evaluation multiplicity for GNU range initializers is not specified.
H-INCOMPLETE-ARRAY-DESIGNATED-BOUND: sparse and range designators do not have a frozen incomplete-array bound rule.
H-CLOSING-EDGE-CLEANUP: statement-expression lifetime closure is required on every exit but the lowering paragraph does not define the cleanup edge form.

G2-VOLATILE-UNION-COPY: section 10.1.3 requires volatile aggregates to lower as memberwise volatile accesses, but a union has overlapping members and the specification provides no selected-member authority. Volatile union copy therefore remains fail-closed rather than reading every overlapping member.
G2-VOLATILE-BIT-FIELD-COPY: section 10.1.3 does not freeze the access width, mask sequence, or trace granularity for a volatile aggregate member that is a bit-field. That form remains fail-closed.

G2-AGGREGATE-CALL-ABI: the specification requires one semantic copy for by-value arguments and returns but does not freeze the hidden return-destination parameter position or deterministic origin identity for caller-owned aggregate temporaries. The implementation uses an address-based internal ABI with the return destination before mem/world tokens and a high-bit function-ordinal origin namespace; no broader ABI claim is made.

P9-STRLEN-LITERAL-EDGE: revision 1.9.27 says a string-literal operand folds to the literal's length but does not freeze whether an embedded zero terminates that length or whether prefixed wide, UTF-16, UTF-32 and UTF-8 literals take the constant path. The sealed evidence and positive claim cover ordinary narrow literals without embedded zeros; no broader oracle-conformance claim is made.

P10-VOID-POINTER-DIFFERENCE-EVOIR: section 10.1.3 requires subtraction of two void pointers with byte scale, while Section 3 has no pointer-difference instruction and the Day-7 lowering profile excludes pointer subtraction. The C-HIR interpreter executes the measured same-object form; lowering remains fail closed rather than inventing an EvoIR operation.

P10-INT128-EXECUTION-BOUNDARY: section 10.1.3 says 128-bit objects are assigned, loaded and stored like any integer object, but the C-HIR and EvoIR scalar value models are still at most 64 bits and the older normative boundary explicitly rejects 128-bit execution. This window proves front-end modifiable-place and compound-assignment typing only; no interpreter or lowering execution claim is made.

P10-NEXT-ENUM-SIGNED-SHIFT: revision 1.9.28 defines completed-list typing for values outside int but does not define whether the GNU enumerator expression 1 << 31 is an integer constant expression or how its mathematical value is obtained without host signed overflow. It is the first error in two lanes at include/linux/skbuff.h:715.
P10-NEXT-BUILTIN-FRAME-ADDRESS: __builtin_frame_address is absent from revision 1.9.28. It is the first error in four lanes across init-do-mounts-initrd and kernel-power-main.

P10-NEXT-POINTER-SIGNEDNESS-CONVERSION: revision 1.9.28 does not freeze the GNU pointer-sign conversion used by .name = value from char * to const unsigned char * inside a compound literal. It is the first E2202 in six lanes across init-do-mounts, mm-mprotect and mm-mincore.
processDeviations: Three constructs were added in implementation commits rather than in the tests-only commit, each discovered by a publication and covered by a test that failed first: record-member declarator lists (adce449), aligned arguments as constant expressions (ed8302b), attribute positions in members, block scope and parameters (eae3e42).

The first real publication reused a stale capture after the observer refused to overwrite it, producing a receipt whose subject commit did not match its run; the publisher now captures per commit and takes the run directory from its own capture (a15872e). The receipt in the tree is from the corrected publisher.
Two RED expectations were corrected by the oracle before implementation: aligned on a typedef may lower alignment (4,1 not 4,4) and a lone packed member gives (8,2) not (8,4).

The typeof-only intermediate commit described by the implementation plan was not made because it would leave one declared workspace test red while the same plan required a green workspace before every production commit; bd9a112 closes both constructs atomically.

The plan's lowering identity fixture used a pointer parameter that the existing allocation manifest rejects even in the spelled-out baseline. The fixture uses an address-taken local pointer instead, preserving the intended volatile-pointer front-end identity check without expanding the pointer-call ABI.

The first dashboard publication attempt was rejected before measurement because the container runtime could not write its state within the sandbox; it was rerun with the same command outside that boundary. A separate relative-evidence-path defect in the publisher was exposed and avoided with the measured absolute evidence path recorded in gate.command.

The _Static_assert lexer token existed but its declaration grammar did not. Scope E requires __builtin_constant_p in that context, so the smallest positive _Static_assert consumer was added without opening its unfrozen negative diagnostic surface.

The final byte-identity pair exposed a previously masked __alignof__ representation difference: a cast of an integer literal lowered differently from the equivalent target-width constant. Lowering now canonicalizes that cast, and all six front-end-only form pairs are byte-identical.

The first asm publication had zero regressions but left six lanes stopped on E2914 because projected record lvalues are represented as checked memory reads. A new regression test failed first, asm output validation was changed to recover the retained MemoryPlace modifiability, and the follow-up publication moved all six lanes without regression.

The first preprocessor publication attempt was refused before any lane because a git worktree does not contain the sealed ignored .toolchain archive and .build reference tree. The five verified commits were fast-forwarded to the clean authoritative root, and the only completed publication ran there against the declared previous run.

Two sandboxed layout invocations stopped at a denied container image-list operation while the shell EXIT cleanup masked the failure as rc 0. They were rejected as evidence; sequential elevated reruns produced explicit 128/128 and 14/14 PASS summaries with zero mismatches.

The declared hash-token property was already green at the RED checkpoint. Because the same instruction also required one tests-only opening commit, the obsolete evocc-cpp compatibility path was removed in the immediately following behavior-neutral production commit instead of falsifying a missing capability or mixing production edits into RED.

The first pasted-token publication was correctly refused: strict one-token re-lexing regressed the GNU comma-elision form , ## __VA_ARGS__ in lib-fdt-wip. A three-case omitted/nonempty/explicitly-empty regression test was added first, the GNU-only rule was implemented, and the repeated publication had zero regressions.

The initial sandboxed layout subject invocation returned no usable evidence because the sealed local container boundary was denied. The authoritative reruns used the same commands with the required container permission and produced explicit 128/128 and 22/22 PASS summaries with zero mismatches.

A first attempt to run the base and attributed layout gates concurrently was rejected because both fail-closed checks share the global container inventory. No result from that attempt was used; the recorded gates are the subsequent sequential 128/128 and 22/22 runs.

macOS provenance scanning made direct execution of workspace test binaries take roughly one minute per target. The recorded workspace and isolated-clone test commands use a temporary runner that copies each already-built binary to /private/tmp and removes only the copy's provenance attribute before execution; focused direct runs and the full semantic results agree.

Three boundary probes (UCN identifier characters in a pp-number, delayed C-token conversion, and numeric-shaped invalid integer tokens in #if) were added after the opening checkpoint. Each was observed RED before its fix and is recorded in the RED diagnostic artifact; they refine the single declared preprocessing-token-paste capability rather than expanding the window.

The invalid differential corpus exposed a semantic split inside the declared pointer-update capability: C-HIR computed a new byte offset without validating the resulting pointer while EvoIR enforced pointer_valid. C-HIR now calls the shared object-memory validity check after source pointer arithmetic, so both interpreters report E3011 beyond one-past.

The first independent-proof fixture yielded a valid zero-region certificate because its only add was rooted in memory and therefore ineligible for P0. A separate pure identity function now forces one non-vacuous scalar rewrite while the same module still exercises loaded-pointer places; evo-proofcheck replays that certificate independently.

Two preprocessing-token dashboard captures were refused at 16/48 observations because they were launched inside the restricted sandbox: every raw lane succeeded, then the Apple container CLI returned Operation not permitted when inspecting the sealed oracle image. Both incomplete captures remain preserved and were not used. The complete publication used the same subject commit and previous-run lineage with the required container permission; it sealed 48/48 observations with zero regressions.

The verbatim statement-expression cohort shape using __auto_type remains declared as a dependency on the compile-time inference window. An active equivalent fixture uses typeof, and no test is disabled.

The earlier boundary test for compound literals was migrated from expecting E2902 to expecting successful parsing in the same semantic commit that retired the diagnostic; the regression test was not deleted.

The first compound-literal dashboard capture was refused after the restricted sandbox denied container inspection and remains preserved as incomplete evidence. Review then found that static compound-literal lowering fabricated an undefined global_addr. A failing regression test was added, the lowerer was changed to fail closed for this unfrozen relocation, and the successful publication was made from the follow-up subject 3a201db.

File-scope compound literals are parsed and executed with static/read-only object semantics, but their EvoIR relocation lowering remains fail-closed because sections 10.1.13 and 3 do not define deterministic unnamed global identity or the required static pointer relocation/provenance representation. No representation was invented.

The initial case-range implementation normalized consecutive ordinary case labels in the parser, which made the new byte-identity test pass but changed a frozen C-HIR fingerprint. The full workspace gate caught it before commit; C-HIR preservation was restored and only lowering now coalesces consecutive label chains after selector conversion.

Revision 1.9.14 referred to an EvoIR unreachable terminator that did not exist in Sections 3 or 9. Production work stopped until the architecture owner supplied revision 1.9.15; the implementation then added the typed trap reason and verified validator, both interpreters, textual round-trip, proof-checker, and eqopt behavior as one semantic unit.

Aggregate copy-initialization is represented by InitAction::CopyAggregate rather than a second aggregate-only expression node. Aggregate expressions retain object addresses; the caller allocates one temporary for each by-value argument, and aggregate returns use one caller-owned hidden destination. This gives exactly one copy at each C semantic boundary and avoids a parallel by-value SSA representation.

Volatile struct copies recursively emit volatile loads and stores in declaration order, while ordinary aggregate copies remain one opaque EvoIR copy. Volatile unions and volatile bit-fields are refused at their named specification gaps instead of inventing overlapping or width-dependent trace semantics.

The G2 publication moved all 28 E2202 aggregate-initializer lanes to E1001 expected-declaration in arch/arm64/include/asm/cmpxchg.h with zero regressions. The new first-error class was retained as unclassified until the parse-closure measurement assigned its concrete declaration forms.

Revision 1.9.17 withdrew the successor-set/E3028 computed-goto contract before production resumed. The tests-only checkpoint was amended first: the front end preserves label addresses and goto *, while the C-HIR interpreter and lowering fail closed with E3029 and no EvoIR instruction is invented.

Rust 1.98 enabled a fixed-size decoder-slice Clippy warning in four pre-existing binary decoders. Commit 5ac26b1 is a behavior-neutral maintenance change that restores the frozen zero-warning gate and is not counted as a parse-closure semantic commit.

The attributable publication after the three C11 declaration forms had zero regressions but did not close stage F1. All 28 parser lanes moved to E2912 in the already-specified kernel __is_constexpr composition; the receipt records every affected unit and leaves F1 OPEN instead of treating first-error movement as acceptance.

The first sealed constant-expression probe was rejected even though its container command returned zero: the read-only filesystem made both compilers fail and the runner lacked set -e. Only the rerun with set -eu, a writable output mount, and bound image/compiler/source/runner digests supplied oracle evidence.

The first complete workspace gate caught an obsolete unit test that accepted int fixed[0] = {}. Revision 1.9.18 requires E2923 for a written zero bound, while int inferred[] = {} remains legal because no bound is written; the test was split to retain both behaviors before the gate was rerun.

The fold-only F1 publication was retained separately from the final array-bound publication. It proves the 28 E2912 lanes moved to __uint128_t; the final revision 1.9.18 publication proves that enforcing E2923 then exposed the zero-bound authority conflict earlier in the same 14 units.

The initialized-VLA path originally anchored E2203 at the initializer while the new eager bound check anchored it at the declarator bound. The focused regression caught this unintended span change; initialized declarations remain on the established initializer validation path while every path now uses the canonical variable-length-object message.

The first revision 1.9.19 dashboard publication attempt was refused when the restricted sandbox denied the local container runtime inspect operation. Its incomplete capture is preserved at .evidence/kernel-dashboard/8402eea-sandbox-refused-20260829T093740Z and was not used; the repeated publication on the same commit and lineage sealed 48/48 observations with zero regressions.

The original unevaluated-operand fixture wrapped sizeof(__typeof_unqual__(side++)) in a void cast, but the existing C-HIR scalar interpreter cannot execute that otherwise unrelated void-cast expression. The GREEN fixture returns side plus the measured sizeof value and subtracts that value, preserving the exact side==0 property without widening K4.

The first K4 publication attempt was refused before lane execution because the isolated worktree lacked a real, project-contained frozen kernel archive; that failed capture is preserved as .evidence/kernel-dashboard/cbf084c-refused-missing-archive. A second run sealed 48/48 observations but the publisher then raised ValueError while relativizing the shared evidence path to the isolated checkout; that capture is preserved as cbf084c-refused-relative-evidence-path. The authoritative third run used real worktree-local evidence, sealed 48/48 observations, and its byte-verified artifacts were copied into the root evidence tree without changing them.

The reviewer supplied address-rooted container_of as the measured scope-M blocker. Eight tests proved that form was defective, but the immediate sealed publication moved zero lanes and bound the actual first errors to call-result-rooted projections. Scope M therefore used three separately published RED/GREEN checkpoints instead of reporting the plausible initial diagnosis as measured fact.

The first sandboxed scope-M publication stopped before measurement because the restricted container boundary could not inspect the sealed oracle image. It is preserved at .evidence/kernel-dashboard/60c64f2-sandbox-refused and is not evidence; the authoritative rerun 20260830T030920Z-23375 used the same subject and previous-run lineage.

The final scope-M publication cleared all 22 invalid-update-operands lanes and exposed 17 uses of the same E2102 code for a different statement-expression-rooted shape. The frozen M gate is defined by exact target/control expression families, so this newly reachable form is recorded as the next frontier rather than silently expanding the completed scope.

Scope L's contract named init-init-task and mm-mincore as unavailable survey units. A baseline produced before the production edit measured only mm-mincore unavailable; init-init-task already completed with E2102 at line 23018. The receipt preserves that measured correction rather than claiming a 2-to-0 movement.

The recovery dashboard retained zero regressions and 2/16 dual-oracle clean parse, but one clang init-do-mounts lane completed at its existing E2102 instead of timing out under the fixed 10-second budget. The receipt records timeout 5-to-4 and E2102 17-to-18, and does not call the complete 48-lane output byte-identical.

Closing the statement-expression place defect removed all 18 matching E2102 lanes, but the next fixed-budget publication timed out on 22 lanes and left dual-oracle clean parse at 2/16. The publisher correctly reports zero classified regressions because every prior lane was already failing, but that predicate is not a progress predicate; the receipt records the throughput boundary explicitly and does not widen the timeout or claim Stage F1 closure.

The first parser-throughput publication was refused after all 16 raw lanes succeeded because the restricted sandbox denied sealed oracle container inspection. Its incomplete capture is preserved at .evidence/kernel-dashboard/1697338-sandbox-refused-20260830T110119Z and is not acceptance evidence. The permission-correct rerun used the same subject and previous-run lineage, retained the 10-second parser budget, sealed 48/48 observations, and converted all 22 prior timeouts into typed first errors with zero regressions.

The first scope-N GREEN publication covered the measured root update index. A deliberate post-GREEN audit then made index++ a child of arithmetic and observed E3007, proving the internal exact-once boundary was too narrow. Commit 270d2d1 scopes mutation permission across the complete generated expression in both interpreter paths; its follow-up publication classified all 48 observations identically with zero regressions.

One pre-commit workspace invocation omitted the established /tmp runner and was interrupted after macOS provenance scanning imposed per-binary delay; it is not acceptance evidence. The recorded canonical all-target locked/offline run completed 988/988 with the runner. A restricted base-layout invocation also returned rc 1 with no evidence and was rejected; the subsequent sequential sealed runs produced 128/128 and 22/22 ORACLE_CONSENSUS.

The scope-O byte-identity fixture initially called an undefined external function, which the EvoIR validator correctly rejects even in the spelled-out control. The fixture was corrected during GREEN to provide a real definition while retaining the inherited extern redeclaration; the RED still failed first at typeof(function) with E1001 and the corrected pair proves no front-end-only form survives.

A post-fix attempt to run the base and attributed layout observers concurrently was rejected because they share one mutable container identity: one failed deleting the other's running container and the other detected a changing image inventory. Neither result was used; fresh sequential runs produced 128/128 and 22/22 ORACLE_CONSENSUS.

The opening P5 RED proved all five conversion contexts at the parser boundary but executed only assignment and truth testing. Inspection during GREEN found that call and return lowering used a separate function-value mapper that rejected function pointers entirely. The semantic commit therefore adds one weighted dual-interpreter execution case covering initialization, assignment, argument, return and comparison; it refines the declared null-conversion capability and does not open a new one.

The first two packed-enum bisection probe attempts were rejected as evidence because the sealed read-only container prevented compiler temporary or output files under /tmp. The accepted third run binds TMPDIR and the executable to the writable evidence mount, records both compiler identities, and obtains identical size/alignment 1/1 results; only that output is cited.

The scope-P7 measurement configuration changed explicitly from the debug subject compiler to the release subject compiler while retaining the 10-second per-TU timeout and four parser jobs. The observer argv, run configuration and receipt all bind that change; it was not represented as a silent timeout increase.

The reported release timing of init-init-task 20.03 seconds versus kernel-bpf-token 1.15 seconds did not reproduce on the frozen byte-identical inputs at exact baseline 30ed2fc: measured medians were 3.09 and 3.11 seconds. That conflict is retained rather than relabelled. Independent sampling and a deterministic scaling RED exposed a real quadratic lexical-tag lookup; the indexed implementation closes that measured defect and yields a 1.07x real-TU ratio.

The initial scope-P8 GREEN implementation rendered and executed the measured answers, but a deliberate corrupted-C-HIR audit found that downstream validation accepted a forged HasAttribute result because its match branch was empty. The corruption test failed first, then consumers were changed to recompute declaration/member identity and written attributes through the shared anonymous-member resolver. The follow-up publication retained all 48 lane classifications with zero regressions.

The first P10 publication at 3975e88 cleared the declared first-error sites but exposed E2102 on a later 128-bit compound assignment in the same checksum function. A verbatim kernel-shape test was observed RED before b24c7ed replaced the simple-assignment exception with a shared wide-integer operand class; the final publication retains the intermediate run in the single dashboard lineage rather than presenting it as completion.

One final workspace invocation accidentally omitted the established /tmp runner and was interrupted after multiple individually green test binaries demonstrated the known macOS provenance delay. It is not evidence. The complete 1038/1038 workspace gate and 1037/1037 isolated all-target replay both used the established runner and exited zero.
